To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
membrane proteins are degraded at axon terminals, in axonal and dendrites, and that this degradation is cargo specific.
membrane protein degradation in dendrites and axons is a regulated process that is spatially and temporally distinct from degradation in the soma.

(1) membrane protein degradation in axons and dendrites occurs in a regulated and cargo specific manner, (2) membrane protein turnover is required for the health and function of neurons, and (3) the molecular mechanisms that control protein turnover in axons and synapses are distinct from the mechanisms that control protein degradation in the cell body
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that underpin protein sorting and degradation in the nervous system.
how the nervous system is organized and how the nervous system develops.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate protein degradation in neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
membrane proteins are degraded at all compartments and subcompartments of neurons, and the mechanisms are diverse and context dependent.
the degradation machinery in neurons is not different from that of non-neuronal cells.
membrane protein turnover and degradation is a complex, highly regulated process that involves a variety of different cellular compartments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the proteasome and the lysosome are involved in membrane protein turnover in neurons.
we have identified a mechanism that is involved in the degradation of the amyloid precursor protein and the prion protein.

we have developed and applied a new approach to the study of the role of protein degradation in neurons and have found that the degradation of membrane proteins in the axon is an important part of normal function and that the degradation of specific membrane proteins in the soma is important for the survival of neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

neurons have evolved mechanisms to selectively degrade specific membrane proteins at distinct subcellular compartments, and that these degradation processes are tightly coupled to the trafficking of membrane proteins.
the degradation of membrane proteins in neurons is highly compartmentalized.
membrane proteins are not only degraded in the cell body but also at axon terminals.
